correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, each excited cell at t>=1 has adjacent refractory predecessor; R/L 21/12 fronts have unique same-direction ancestors and only move at unit speed; opposing ancestral fronts on a cycle have forward distance d<=n-2 and cannot co-survive past floor(d/2) rounds; by time floor(n/2)+1 at most one orientation persists; one more step produces a rotating pure wave or zero. Single initial excited cell gives matching all-zero first hitting time floor(n/2)+2. Verified against entire 3^n state graphs n=3..11 and local front constraints n=3..8, 2000 additional random configurations.

value.rationale: A sharp uniform finite-time entrance bound for every initial state of a standard excitable automaton quantifies worst-case relaxation and makes finite state-space certification possible without enumerating 3^n configurations. It closes the nonconservative winding case not supplied by the cited diameter synchronization theorem; both a sharp exponent and an explicit extremizer matter for the naturally defined system.
